gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the shopper's real case into one comparable number: how many watts the laptop port still gets once a phone is plugged in. On EPICKA's Air the advertised 65 W drops to 40 W, TESSAN's WTA07 rates only C3 at 65 W and doesn't publish what it delivers when other ports are busy, and EPICKA's TA-105 Pro rates one USB-C port at 70 W but doesn't publish a multi-port split.
standout_why: I compared against Kit Authority (cited in 2 chats), TreksSavvy and mobileplustech. I couldn't open WIRED (blocked) or Best Buy (timed out). Kit Authority already has the WTA07 figures (65 W on C3 alone, 15 W on each other port, no combined total) and the TA-105 Max split (35+20+20 W), but it covers neither the TA-105 Pro, the Air nor the WTA09. TreksSavvy already has the Air dropping to 40 W + 15 W, from the manual. mobileplustech gives no split for any travel adapter. Each fact exists on some page, but no page puts the 'laptop watts with a phone attached' figure side by side for the three products ChatGPT recommends. The two figures that would make this new, the WTA09 and TA-105 Pro splits, I could not source.
decides: It weakens the case for the EPICKA Air, which ChatGPT called 'best overall' in one chat: by EPICKA's own manual as quoted by TreksSavvy, it charges a laptop at 40 W, not 65 W, while a phone is also charging, and the maker's store page says only that it 'keeps 20W PD even during multi-port charging'. On TESSAN the 65 W is on one dedicated port, C3 (WTA07 per Kit Authority), but no source I opened says whether it holds 65 W while other ports are in use. So the pick is still undecided until the WTA09 and TA-105 Pro split tables are read. The page's table should have a 'laptop W with a phone attached' column, and its footnote should be that 'up to 65 W' is a figure for that port alone.
